blocks.text: Size matters for pull time, cold starts and patch surface, but correctness comes first: every removal must keep the app's runtime dependencies intact.

items: Don't install what you don't need: CPU-only torch (`--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu`) drops gigabytes of CUDA.
Clean caches in the same layer, or use cache mounts.

rows: Entrypoint scripts and shell CMD fail

blocks.text: If baked in, put that layer before `COPY app` so code changes don't re-push weights.
Verify in CI with `docker run --rm img python -c "import app.main"`: it catches missing shared libraries before deploy.

Q: "Your FastAPI image is 4 GB. What do you do?" A: "Check docker history: usually CUDA torch on a CPU service, a full base, build tools and caches. Switch to CPU wheels, a slim multi-stage build, same-layer cleanup and a strict .dockerignore, then smoke-test imports."

items: Biggest win: don't install unneeded packages.
Keep runtime libs and CA certificates.
